audit.text: The repository tracks 3,340 files and 148 MB, of which 2,061 are HTML pages. The canonical build publishes one desk; the rest is accumulated archive.

audit.evidence: pipeline/build.py ARCHIVE has 22 entries; 78 desk directories exist
audit.text: 78 eight-hex desk directories are committed but only 22 are registered in the ARCHIVE list of pipeline/build.py. The other 56 are in the repository and in git history but unreachable from the published site.

The canonical snapshot under data/current reports captured_listings 108 but current_listings 0, upcoming_exact 0, priced_matches 0 and originated_markets 0. The canonical pipeline is capturing OLBG rows and then resolving none of them as current, so the canonical dataset has never produced a priced match.
data/current/audit.json is 10.0 MB, the largest tracked file, and is rewritten by every refresh. It makes the repository diff noisy and slows every clone.

COORDINATION.md runs to 7,440 lines. Seven different sessions have recorded themselves as owning "the canonical front door" and 39 lines mention "final integration". The convention in section 0.2 (one pinned branch per session) is sound; the bookkeeping has outgrown the file.

The committed root carries 20 top-level HTML pages and the published artifact is 25 pages, so the front door and the artifact are not the same shape. A reader following a root link can land on a page the canonical build does not regenerate.

All local links across the nine primary root pages resolve on disk. 42 distinct local HTML targets are linked from index.html and every one exists. No broken local link was found in this session's scan.

No compiled artefacts are tracked: zero __pycache__ or .pyc files are in the index, and .gitignore already covers _site, node_modules and raw response bodies. The transient-tool convention is being followed.

audit.text: Peer desks in this repository publish tipped-share percentages as confidence and some label OLBG prices as originating here. A member tip share is a vote share. This desk reproduces tip shares verbatim and never uses one as a probability.

.github/workflows/current-pages.yml is the only publishing workflow and it builds from pipeline/build.py on main. evidence-pages.yml is manual-dispatch only, so it cannot race the canonical deploy. That arrangement is correct.

flags.text: OLBG returned the literal text "No tips found." on the golf hub, so no golf market was available to price. No PGA or DP World Tour fixture was read this session either, so the golf row is empty on both the discovery and the official side.
OLBG returned "No tips found." on the snooker hub. No WST match page was read, so no snooker fixture or price appears.

OLBG returned "No tips found." on the baseball hub and the MLB schedule feed returned zero games for 25 October. The next MLB fixture is World Series game 3 on 26 October, which is listed but unpriced: the official feed publishes no starting pitcher, and no season record was read.
OLBG listed only three outright markets for 2027 (State of Origin, Super League, NRL). No upcoming Rugby League match market existed to price.

OLBG's basketball feed listed five events, all Korea KBL or Poland PLK. It listed no NBA market at all, even though the NBA played seven games on 25 October. The five NBA games priced here are official NBA fixtures and are not OLBG markets.

No NBA pick is issued. The only official input is a win-loss record two or three games old; the originated money line for every NBA game sits between -150 and +125, within a few points of a league-average home-court price. Recommending a side on that evidence would be a coin toss dressed as analysis, so the prices are published and the picks are withheld.

Four of the five NHL games on 25 October were fully captured. The fifth (game id 2026020184, Rogers Arena) was truncated mid-record, so neither club nor its start time was read on an official page. It is listed with the gap marked and is not priced.

No injury report, lineup, starter or availability list was read for any fixture. No prediction names an injured or returning player, because none was confirmed. This is a deliberate blank, not an oversight.

No player-level statistic was captured for any of the nine priced fixtures. The 25 October NHL goal scorers are not published until games finish, and no skater or goaltender page was read. Predictions therefore cite club-level figures only.

The PDC tournament page returned a cookie-consent wall and no draw, schedule or result was readable. OLBG lists four European Championship matches and gives times that conflict with nothing confirmed officially, so no darts price is issued.

Both www.premiershiprugby.com/league-table and the newer www.premrugby.com/fixtures-results returned no server-rendered fixture or standings data (one 404, one client-rendered shell). The Harlequins v Saracens and La Rochelle v Bordeaux markets OLBG lists are therefore unpriced.

The ICC fixtures page returned every card as the placeholder "loading", so no Pakistan v England or South Africa domestic fixture could be confirmed officially. Eight OLBG cricket markets are listed unpriced.

Formula 1 confirms round 18, the United States Grand Prix, runs 23-25 October and is marked LIVE, and the calendar publishes round winners for rounds 1-7. It does not publish the grid in a form that was read, and the drivers page rendered names without the points column. A race-winner price without the grid would be invented, so the race is listed unpriced.

OLBG's tennis feed lists Leylah Fernandez in two separate matches on different days (against Elena Rybakina and against Himeno Sakatsume). Both rows are reproduced exactly as OLBG published them. One of the two is almost certainly a stale listing, but which one cannot be determined from OLBG alone.

Nine of the fifteen handball rows show "Tie" as the most-tipped money-line outcome, which is unusual for a three-way market. It is reported exactly as OLBG published it and is not treated as a signal.
OLBG's Gaelic rows publish a handicap selection (for example "Nemo Rangers +1.50") but no market name, so the market column is blank for that sport rather than guessed.
OLBG listed a single greyhound race (11:04 Doncaster) with one member tip on the dog Snowfall. No GBGB racecard, trap draw or form line was read, so nothing is priced.
OLBG lists fifteen volleyball fixtures across Italian, Polish, Turkish, German, French and Finnish leagues. No official league page for any of them was read this session, so none is priced.

OLBG prints relative day labels ("Tomorrow 19:07") with no stated timezone. The labels only line up with the official UTC start times if they are resolved in US Eastern, where it was still 24 October when this desk captured them. Every relative label here is reproduced verbatim and never converted.

Where an OLBG time can be compared with an official start, it runs about seven minutes late: MTL @ WPG is 19:07 on OLBG and 23:00Z (19:00 ET) on the NHL feed; NYI @ DAL is 18:07 against 22:00Z (18:00 ET). OLBG times are therefore not used as start times.
NBA start times are published as local Eastern tip times only. The UTC column is arithmetic from the published ET time (EDT, UTC-4) and is labelled as derived, not as something the NBA published.

Fourteen of the fifteen brief sports have no priced match. That is the evidence cap, not a quota: a price needs an official fixture plus an official current-season figure for both sides, and for thirteen sports at least one of those was not readable from an official publisher today.

predictions.nhl-2026020180: Back the Florida Panthers on the money line when they visit the Chicago Blackhawks at the United Center. Florida are 5-4-2 for 12 points, with 31 goals scored and 34 conceded in 11 games, and they are 3-3-2 on the road with a last-ten line of 4-4-2. Chicago are 3-7-0 on six points, have scored only 22 goals in ten games and have conceded 40, a total bettered only by Vancouver and San Jose in the published table. The Blackhawks are 0-4-0 away and have lost their last two, so the road side is the selection.
predictions.nhl-2026020181: Dallas Stars to beat the New York Islanders at the American Airlines Center. Dallas are 6-3-1 for 13 points and have conceded only 17 goals in ten games, the lowest goals-against figure anywhere in the published league table, while scoring 26. They have won four straight and are 3-2-0 at home. The Islanders arrive at 5-3-2 on 12 points with 29 scored and 23 conceded, a 1-2-1 road record and an overtime defeat in their most recent game.
predictions.nhl-2026020183: The selection is the Colorado Avalanche to win at the Nashville Predators. Colorado are 6-4-1 for 13 points and have scored 47 goals in 11 games, an average of 4.27 per game that is matched by Vegas and bettered only by Edmonton's 49 in the Western Conference, while conceding 34. Nashville are 3-3-4 on 10 points with 25 scored and 33 conceded, and four of their ten games have finished as overtime or shootout defeats. The Predators are 2-2-1 at home and carry a last-ten line of 3-3-4 into the game.
